notes:
- (1.0.36) Scopes zoom again: a scoped weapon (its own scope or a scope mod) zooms when you aim, while iron sights still keep your field of view
- (1.0.36) The GAME & ADD-ONS panel scrolls with the mouse wheel when it has more than fits
- (1.0.35) Fixed: setup froze when FIRST TIME START-UP, WHAT'S IN IT, KEYBINDS or YOUR MODS was pressed
- (1.0.35) Updates now come from the GitHub Releases page (the old place stays as a backup)
- (1.0.34) New here? FIRST TIME START-UP walks you through playing together, from MAKE IT WORK to joining your friend's world (it opens by itself after your first setup); WHAT'S IN IT lists everything the mod adds, and KEYBINDS lists every key that works in your game
- (1.0.34) WORLD: pick New Vegas or Tale of Two Wastelands (if you have TTW installed) right in setup - TTW's plugins come out of or go back into your load order, nothing is deleted, and each world keeps its own saves
- (1.0.34) YOUR MODS: play together with all your mods - from the game folder, Vortex (setup checks it has deployed), or Mod Organizer 2 (PLAY starts the game through it, with your whole profile). Everyone needs the same mods in the same order, or playing together breaks
- (1.0.34) Fixed: with Mod Organizer 2, Mojave Enhanced is now really switched on in its load order
- (1.0.34) Only Mojave Enhanced's own files ship now: the F8 menu uses the game's fonts (or Windows' Consolas)
- (1.0.33) New Vegas's own look for everything: trading is the game's own message box (both offers and who's ready, updated as they change - press E on your friend to see it), notifications are the game's own again and no longer pile up, and the F8 menu, chat and listen-in subtitles are drawn the way the game draws its menus, in its own fonts from your game
- (1.0.33) Fixed: a crash when a friend got out of your truck (their hit body was made again too soon)
- (1.0.33) Smoother: no hitch getting into a car, and less stutter when a friend's fight keeps coming into view
- (1.0.33) Your friend's world is always the one they have now: an old copy of it is never loaded again (you go home with what you earned and come straight back into the current one)
- (1.0.33) Quest items never come home from a friend's world - the flagged ones and the ones a quest depends on (like the Platinum Chip) - they're handed to the host; your guns and armour still come home
- (1.0.32) Riding with a friend: you both sit at the right height in their truck, and their truck rides on its suspension on your screen too - wheels up and down, steering, the launch and the bass shake, as the driver sees it
- (1.0.32) Friends see your gun handling on your body - the sway, the kick, the flip and the wobble - even while you play in first person
- (1.0.32) Downed is a real knock-out now: you go limp like a knocked-out companion and stay down, you can't turn, and friends see your body lie as it fell
- (1.0.32) Our notifications show at once and a newer one of the same kind replaces the old (the radio's volume keeps up as you turn it); chat lines stay
- (1.0.32) No IP addresses: the join message shows only the name, and the log hides them
- (1.0.31) Trading is a live window now: press E at a friend and you both see both offers side by side. 1 changes your offer, 2 says you're ready, 3 gives yours as a gift (whoever started), 4 calls it off - the swap happens when you're both ready
- (1.0.31) What your shots break - Sunny's bottles and the like - breaks for your friends too
- (1.0.31) A quest's enemies the host's world brings out show up for guests too (the tutorial's geckos)
- (1.0.31) The host's conversations count: near the host, a conversation the game starts on a guest by itself closes, and a guest's choices don't change the host's world
- (1.0.31) If a guest's copy of a quest goes its own way while the host is with them, they take a quick trip home with what they earned and come straight back into the host's world as it is
- (1.0.31) Nothing gets lost between your games any more: every kill, quest step and trade is sent again until your friend's game says it got it, however long the fight or the conversation
- (1.0.31) Playing together keeps going while you're in a menu or a conversation: your friends keep moving on your screen and what they do still reaches you
- (1.0.31) Listen in: when a friend within 10 m talks to someone, what's said shows as subtitles on your screen - you're not pulled into the conversation and your game isn't changed
- (1.0.30) Shared XP: every bit of XP you earn - kills, lockpicks, hacks, new places, speech checks, quests - goes to friends within 100 m of you too (a quest step you both did isn't paid twice)
- (1.0.30) Your own loot: when something dies while you play together, each of you finds your own roll of its loot on your own copy of the body - you can both loot it. Chests stay shared. Companions' things are never touched
- (1.0.30) /ranges in chat: rings on the ground show 100 m (shared XP), 60 m (the host's people around a guest) and 2 m (getting a downed friend up), with each friend's name and distance over them
- (1.0.30) Trade with a friend: walk up and press E ("Talk" and their name), put your offer in the box, then give it to them or ask for a trade - nothing changes hands until a gift arrives or you both accept, and a decline, a cancel or a dropped connection gives everyone their things back
- (1.0.30) Vendors match in every world: what one of you buys or sells changes that vendor's stock and caps for everyone
- (1.0.30) Fixed: a crash when a friend shot right after the host loaded a save
- (1.0.30) When the host loads another save, friends in their world go home with what they earned and come straight back into the new one
- (1.0.29) Smoother for a guest in a friend's world: less work every frame for a guest below the host's level, and for your friend's hit body and the enemies drawn from their game
- (1.0.29) People round you act on a quest step from your friend's game straight away (Sunny no longer stands out front while the quest has moved on)
- (1.0.29) The log says what playing together costs, part by part, so any slowdown left can be pinned down
- (1.0.28) Safe in a friend's world: loading a save, starting a new game or quitting to the main menu there keeps everything you earned (written down the moment before), takes it home to your own character and puts you back in your friend's world. A save you make there is renamed "MMW-Friend world - ..." so it's never mistaken for one of your own
- (1.0.28) No freeze when many of your friend's enemies come into view at once
- (1.0.27) Fixed: people near a friend (Sunny, Cheyenne, Easy Pete...) dropping dead in the host's game - a friend's game took its copy of them, held still to be drawn from the host's game, for a dead one
- (1.0.27) Fixed: the game crawling (10 fps) for a guest in VATS
- (1.0.27) Joining: whenever you and your friend are on the same version with the same mods, you go into the host's world by itself - when you join, and again whenever you're back in your own game while still connected (a session that never finished goes home with what you earned first). If versions or mods differ you're told once and play side by side. Chat commands work in capitals too (/JOIN)
- (1.0.27) Fixed: a friend's left forearm (the Pip-Boy arm) sometimes missing
- (1.0.26) Chat is our own now: press Enter (and let go), type, Enter sends, Esc closes. The box shows low on the left; the game's keys are off while you type
- (1.0.26) The same load order on every PC: setup switches on the game's own DLC files in your Data folder and puts them in Bethesda's order, other mods after, Mojave Enhanced last (a friend's DLCs were off, so your games never matched and joining the host's world was refused) - press MAKE IT WORK once
- (1.0.26) Fixed: people near a friend (Sunny and Cheyenne going out of the saloon door) could drop dead in the host's game
- (1.0.25) Chat: the box is big enough to show its OK button now - type, then click OK to send
- (1.0.25) Downed: you're knocked to the ground and stay there until a friend gets you up or you use a stimpak
- (1.0.25) Fixed: joining could kill enemies in the host's game that were only dead in the guest's save; an enemy dead in your game no longer stands up again because it lives in your friend's
- (1.0.25) Fixed: a friend could turn into a tangled ball stuck in the floor (their body's numbers went bad after being downed)
- (1.0.25) The report (setup > REPORT) lists the mods your load order names that aren't in the game, and finds them in Vortex's or Mod Organizer's folders if they're installed but not deployed
- (1.0.24) Chat works: press Enter, type, press Enter to send (the box used to close before you could type) - /ff on or off, /join, /leave and /name work again
- (1.0.24) Friendly fire really hurts now (hits on friends were counted but did no damage); a hit that would kill still puts you down
- (1.0.24) Kills you make on a friend's enemies count in their game too: no more enemies left alive on a sliver of health
- (1.0.24) Joining a friend in setup takes you into their world by itself after a few seconds (you need the same mods; if they differ you're told and play side by side). /leave takes you home
- (1.0.24) Shorter hitch after loading; everyone needs 1.0.24 for the friendly-fire and kill fixes
- (1.0.23) Third person, the whole body: your feet stand on the ground you're on - steps, slopes, rocks - with the soles tilted to it, and your hips go down to the lower foot. Standing, your feet stay planted and step as you turn
- (1.0.23) Free look, always on: standing still, your head (and a little of your chest) follows the camera while your body stays put; moving, aiming or firing turns you to face where you look, smoothly
- (1.0.23) The body leans into starts, running and turns, forward up hills and back down them (the steeper, the more) and to the high side across a slope - not on stairs, and small rocks don't rock it
- (1.0.23) Movement eases in: setting off, going from walk to run to sprint (and back down) and turning back on yourself take a moment, soft but noticeable
- (1.0.23) The person: breathing (harder after sprinting and when hurt), weight shifting from leg to leg, now and then a shrug, a rolled shoulder or a neck stretch, arms that sway and swing with your moves, a dip when you land, a flinch when you're hit, a glance at people nearby
- (1.0.23) Changes of pose (crouching, standing up, drawing, aiming, starting and stopping) blend smoothly instead of snapping
- (1.0.23) F8 has a line for each of it: foot placement, body lean, body bank, hill lean, hill side lean, animation blend time, head look, breath/weight/arms and movement acceleration. You can still play together with friends on 1.0.22
- (1.0.22) Fixed: friends are drawn as themselves again, not as copies of you
- (1.0.22) Fixed: a friend joining no longer lifts you into the sky
- (1.0.22) New, being tested: join your friend's world. While playing together, press Enter and type /join: the host's world comes over to you and you play in it as your own character. /leave takes you back to your own game with the XP, caps, items, karma, reputation and places you earned there. Quest steps done within 100 m of each other count in your own game too. If the host leaves, you get 60 seconds, then you go home with what you earned.
- (1.0.22) New, being tested: death is real but avoidable while you play together. What would kill you puts you down: a friend has 20 seconds to get you up (E), or you use a stimpak (1). Nobody in time and you die - 20 caps lost (none if you have none) - and you're back on your feet next to a friend, or at the last safe place you stood. The game is never loaded again, so nothing since your last save is lost
- (1.0.22) New, being tested: friendly fire. Your shots and blows hurt your friends (the host decides: type /ff on or /ff off in chat; on by default), and the people fighting your friend in your game hurt them too
- (1.0.22) New, being tested: one shared world. In the host's world the people around you are the host's (same people, same places), deaths near either of you happen for both, and doors you open, close or unlock open, close or unlock for everyone
- (1.0.22) In a friend's world, if you're a lower level than the host your health and your damage are raised to the host's (your guns stay as they are); everything you gain yourself takes the same off the boost, and none of it comes home. A host is never raised: play with gods if you like
- (1.0.22) While you're in a friend's world, the game's autosaves and quicksave (F5) are off, so none of your own save slots get the session written over them
- (1.0.22) Your mods are compared with your friend's when you play together, and it tells you which differ (joining their world needs the same mods)
- (1.0.22) Playing together works from the very start: no more waiting until Doc Mitchell's. A guest joining a host who's still in Doc's house stands beside them and gets the same character creation (face, name, SPECIAL, traits, tag skills) for their own character, which comes home as made
- (1.0.21) Fixed: Steam's "Application load error 5:0000065434" when the game starts - it's started through Steam again
- (1.0.21) The intro skipping is gone: the game starts as it normally does (lStewieAl's skip-intro and continue-without-asking settings are put back off)
- (1.0.21) Playing together, safer: a new join code (MMW2-...) every time you host, which stops working after 12 hours; the host lets each friend in (F6) or refuses them (F7); the router's port closes again after 4 hours. Everyone needs 1.0.21 to play together.
- (1.0.21) Panic key: Ctrl+Alt+End frees the mouse, ends playing together and closes a frozen game
- (1.0.21) The pickups: a real steering wheel in the cab, and your companion and friends ride along in the seats
- (1.0.21) The game fills your whole monitor (at your screen's own size; windowed, it's a borderless window)
- (1.0.21) Your New Vegas saves are in one list again, whichever game you pick
- (1.0.21) Fixed: the view (FOV) is put back to your setting after loads, conversations and menus, and conversations no longer zoom in
- (1.0.21) Fixed: a short freeze a few seconds after loading; the F8 menu sometimes not showing
- (1.0.21) A frozen game now says in its log where it's stuck (it goes in the report)
- (1.0.20) Drive the wasteland's own pickup trucks: walk up to one (two sit outside Goodsprings) and press G. It's built on your PC from your own game files, wheels that turn and steer on their own suspension; it's yours from then on
- (1.0.20) The dropkick: sprinting, jump and right-click with your weapon away - a two-footed flying kick that sends people sprawling (never kills them), lands you on your back and you get up again
- (1.0.20) Playing together: friends are really drawn as themselves now (1.0.19's look didn't take on most PCs) and a friend's body no longer carries your Pip-Boy (a crash opening the Pip-Boy)
- (1.0.20) Parkour: your own body no longer shows a second time during wall kicks
- (1.0.19) Playing together: friends look like themselves - their own face, hair, body and the armour and clothes they wear, instead of copies of you. Everyone needs 1.0.19 to see it.
- (1.0.19) Parkour: no more second body during a vault, mantle, climb or wall kick; friends see you do the move on your one body
- (1.0.18) The sprint and parkour are back: hold Shift to sprint, double-tap for a tactical sprint; Space at a ledge vaults, mantles or climbs, and kicks off walls
- (1.0.18) Fixed: after VATS kills in third person the first-person key could stop working
- (1.0.17) Fixed: killing someone in a fight could throw you out of the world (into a rock, far away) - and a crash that came with it
- (1.0.17) The F8 weapon feel menu looks like the game's own HUD: your HUD colour, real lettering, glow and scanlines
- (1.0.16) A fresh install no longer stops at the end with "No cars were built" (vanilla stable builds none on purpose)
- (1.0.16) Mojave Most Wanted is now Mojave Enhanced: Fallout: New Vegas, enhanced. Your saves, settings and the mod's files carry on as they were; the desktop shortcut gets the new name.
- (1.0.16) Set the name your friends see in setup: click NAME, type, press Enter
- (1.0.16) Playing together: friends hold their guns in their hands; their shots show a muzzle flash, light up the area and leave a bullet streak; their bodies lean round cover and into strafes in first person too; everyone's version is checked on joining. Everyone needs 1.0.15 to play together.
- (1.0.16) Playing together: the game keeps running when you tab out (no more dropping out of the session); quick load (F9) is off while in a session, and loading a game no longer crashes
- (1.0.16) Third person: the shoulder swap (X) glides again
- (1.0.14) F8 opens the weapon feel menu: smooth sliders (0-300%) for gun inertia, sway, kick, view recoil, camera shake and roll, the shot's zoom kick, corner-lean speed and the third-person body; saved, applied at once
- (1.0.14) Third person: the body leans round cover and into strafes (aimed too), carries the gun's weight; camera shake and a little roll; X swaps the camera to the other shoulder
- (1.0.14) Third person, aiming: a small X in the crosshair when the wall right in front of your barrel would take the shot
- (1.0.14) Each shot lights up its surroundings for a moment; a small zoom kick on each shot
- (1.0.14) Contextual aiming is smoother and holds you round the corner longer; no more split-second freezes crossing the map
- (1.0.14) PLAY copes with a Fallout.ini that's read-only or held by OneDrive
- (1.0.13) For now PLAY starts vanilla stable: New Vegas with the engine fixes and our gun handling only (inertia, sway, recoil, contextual aiming); no cars. More opens up in later updates.
- (1.0.13) In game: U turns our gun handling on or off, O turns smooth aiming on or off; both switch at once and are remembered. Vanilla stable keeps its own saves.
- (1.0.13) Setup copes with a read-only Fallout.ini
- (1.0.11) PLAY WITHOUT CARS is always there as an on/off button (before, only when Need for Speed was missing)
- (1.0.11) Local add-ons saved by Windows PowerShell show their button again
- (1.0.10) Playing together: guns sit in friends' hands and bodies no longer stretch (the whole skeleton is shared, sized as theirs); every shot heard in time; dropped items show for everyone; containers are shared (what one takes is gone for all); you see the enemies fighting a friend, and kills are shared; chat with Enter, and /name YourName sets the name friends see. Everyone needs 1.0.10 to play together.
- (1.0.10) Undo everything removes every trace: the shortcut, the launcher and its files, our logs and setup itself
- (1.0.9) Playing together: friends move 1:1 with their own animations, hold their guns and you hear their shots; parked cars stay put for friends; ride in a friend's passenger seat (G near the car, or the driver presses I); dropped items are shared. Everyone needs 1.0.9 to play together.
- (1.0.9) The last run's log is MojaveMostWanted-previous.log; a crash also leaves MojaveMostWanted-crash.log
- (1.0.7) Dying no longer crashes the game: out of the car, and everything of ours lets go of you
- (1.0.6) Weapon handling: gun inertia, hip and aimed recoil, wobble, quicker reloads and a crash guard; smooth aim-in (setup turns it on in lStewieAl's Tweaks and kNVSE)
- (1.0.6) Cover aiming: lean, rise or dip to see past cover; blind fire over or round close cover
- (1.0.4) PLAY WITHOUT CARS sets up everything but the cars; (1.0.3) never an older plugin over a newer one
